review_candidates.description: What we are building Mimica is an AI-powered process intelligence platform enabling enterprises and individuals to reclaim their most precious resource: time. We've all seen repetitive tasks and redundant processes quietly drain productivity and creativity. Not because companies don’t want to become more efficient, but because they don’t know where to start. Mimica automatically analyzes your team’s work, then generates the AI agents to execute it. Our software turns everyday work into data-backed decisions, helping companies remove process bottlenecks, automate the right tasks, and upskill teams with precision and confidence. We’ve raised $26 million in Series B financing and are scaling fast. Backed by investors including Khosla Ventures and Paladin Capital, our proprietary AI technology is trusted by Fortune 500 companies to accelerate transformation. Mimica is recognized as a Top 100 AI Start-up by Accel and an industry Leader by the Everest Group. Our team Behind our platform is a team of exceptionally talented people, remote-first and globally distributed across 16+ countries. We're looking for curious, collaborative people excited to solve complex problems. You'll join a fast-paced environment built on high ownership, bottom-up thinking, and transparent, open communication – helping some of the world's leading organizations transform the way work gets done with AI. Your mission Mimica is growing fast, and so is the demand on our Platform Team. As Head of Platform, you will lead a lean but highly capable team that is the backbone of every engineering squad in the company, and you will own the infrastructure strategy, including all AI infrastructure, as we scale. The Platform team services the entire engineering organisation: keeping environments healthy, unblocking teams, building the infrastructure that lets everyone else move faster, and working with teams regarding SRE topics and developer experience too. As you work with us, the role will develop into designing Mimica’s infrastructure strategy at scale. The team has 4 engineers today, around 6 by the end of the year, and 10+ in 2027, so the role has the potential to grow into a “manager of managers” level as the company grows. This is a role with real scope: expanding to multi-region and physically separated database environments, supporting Mimica’s first installable infrastructure component for enterprise, and owning FinOps. One day you are defining the standard menu of deployment options for enterprise customers, the next you are in a security review or an architecture decision on AI infrastructure. We are looking for leaders with either an application development or a systems/infrastructure background. What matters more than your origin story is your hands-on credibility with Kubernetes, IaC, and cloud platforms, your ability to lead engineers and other leaders, and your ability to collaborate closely with Product, ML, Security, Sales and Customer Success. If you want to work in a place where your contributions are visible, your scope is broad, and the problems are real, this is the role for you. Part of your day-to-day Own Mimica's infrastructure strategy and the platform roadmap across all products, with the final call on cloud architecture, deployment models, infra vendors and platform standards. Lead and grow the Platform team: Manage existing Platform and SREs, plan headcount, set goals and metrics, and design the sub-team split (Cloud & Developer Platform, Reliability & SRE, AI Infrastructure) as the team grows. Own all AI infrastructure, including training and serving infra, MLOps tooling, Vertex and model access. Maintain Mimica’s DevEx culture - improve agency for product teams without compromising on compliance, create paved roads for deployments, and identify pain points as they arise. Own the infra and LLM budget, forecast and unit economics, including cost attribution by product and customer and the GCP relationship. Own reliability across engineering: SLOs, on-call model, incident process, postmortems, DR testing and capacity planning. Own the CI/CD and developer platform, infrastructure-as-code (Terraform, ArgoCD, Crossplane) and observability standards (Honeycomb, Grafana, Loki). Work with the Platform PM, your peer, to define client needs and turn them into the platform roadmap. Act as the named technical owner for infrastructure in enterprise deals and security reviews, joining high-stakes sales and client calls and coaching your team to take the rest. Guide the craft mentors for infrastructure, MLOps and Python engineering, and set engineering-wide standards for reliability, on-call, CI/CD and craft. Report monthly platform health and costs to leadership, and lead the infrastructure part of technical due diligence. Requirements Proven experience leading engineers, ideally including managing a team lead or other managers, and growing a team through hiring and sub-team design. Solid hands-on experience with Kubernetes, whether on GKE (preferred), EKS, OnPrem, or another managed Kubernetes service, across multiple regions. Proven experience with infrastructure-as-code as a core part of your platform, such as Terraform, and with ArgoCD or a comparable GitOps tool. A track record in owning reliability: setting SLOs and SLAs, running on-call, leading incident response and postmortems, and testing disaster recovery. Observability experience with at least one major platform: Honeycomb, Datadog, Grafana, or New Relic. Comfortable with code, and able to review architecture and prototypes hands-on. Experience owning an infrastructure budget, including cloud cost attribution, forecasting and cloud-provider relationships. Experience designing deployment models for enterprise customers (single tenant, regional, data residency) and supporting security reviews and contracted SLAs. Background in startups or scale-ups: you are used to ambiguity, moving fast, and wearing multiple hats. Strong communication and collaboration skills: you can translate infrastructure complexity into clear language for engineers, executives and clients, and you know when to say no to bespoke requests. Bonus / Nice to have Familiarity with Crossplane, or a similar product like Config Connector. Experience with Temporal for workflow orchestration. Security and compliance experience, particularly supporting SOC 2. Experience supporting a funding round, including technical due diligence. What we offer 💰 Generous compensation + stock options - aligned with our internal framework, market data, and individual skills. 🏢 Distributed work: Work from anywhere - fully remote, in our hubs, or a mix. 💻 Company-issued laptop, remote setup stipend, and co-working budget 📍 Flexible schedules and location ☀️ Ample paid time off, in addition to local public holidays 🍼 Enhanced parental leave 🧘‍♀️ Health & retirement benefits 📖 Annual learning & development budget 🌴 Annual workaways and regular virtual & in-person socials 🌍 Opportunity to contribute to groundbreaking projects that shape the future of work Note : Some benefits may vary depending on location and role ⚠️ Mimica will only contact candidates from an @mimica.ai email address. We do not request banking or sensitive personal information during the recruiting process.

review_candidates.company: Boys & Girls Clubs of King County
review_candidates.description: The Chief Administrative Officer (CAO) leads the business operations of Boys & Girls Clubs of King County, with responsibility for Finance, Human Resources, Information Technology, as well as facilities and real estate, contracts and risk management. A member of the senior leadership team reporting to the President & CEO, the CAO builds the enterprise-wide operational systems, financial discipline and infrastructure the organization needs to serve youth across all Club sites and to grow. Job Summary We are looking for an accomplished executive to serve as our Chief Administrative Officer and a trusted thought partner to the President & CEO. The ideal candidate is a proven second-in-command with strong financial acumen, a solid understanding of HR, and a track record of leading organizational transformation. Above all, we are seeking a leader with exceptionally strong operational skills and experience, who will strengthen our processes and ensure consistent compliance with our policies across the organization. Our most significant opportunity is in enterprise-wide operational systems: the CAO will assess, design and implement the integrated systems, processes and controls that allow the organization to operate efficiently and scale. The goal is to strengthen organizational effectiveness and position the organization for continued growth and impact. The CAO leads a team of approximately 12 staff through the Director of Finance, Director of Human Resources and leaders of IT, Business Analytics and administrative functions, and oversees an annual operating budget of approximately $28M. RESPONSIBILITIES: Strategic Leadership & Transformation Serve as a strategic partner to the President & CEO and translate organizational priorities into coordinated action within and across departments. Prepare and present timely financial, operational and strategic information to the CEO, the Board and its committees, including the finance and audit committees. Lead enterprise-wide transformation: assess systems, structures and processes, and drive change with a focus on alignment, communication, accountability and sustainable adoption. Set goals for each department and its leader; recruit, guide, develop and evaluate the performance of direct reports. Enterprise Operational Systems Assess, design and implement integrated enterprise-wide operational systems, processes and infrastructure that enable the organization to operate efficiently and scale. Lead the selection, implementation and adoption of core enterprise platforms (e.g., financial/ERP, HRIS and payroll, data and reporting) and integrate them across departments and Club sites. Establish standard operating procedures, clear process ownership and performance metrics across operational functions. Strengthen operational processes across the organization, identifying gaps and inefficiencies and putting in place consistent, well-documented practices. Ensure compliance with organizational policies and procedures across all departments and Club sites, establishing the internal controls, monitoring and accountability needed to sustain it. Lead the regular review and updating of organizational policies so they remain current, clear and consistently applied. Evaluate the appropriate use of internal resources, outsourcing and strategic partnerships to deliver effective, cost-efficient services. Finance Lead the finance department through the Director of Finance, including accounting, financial planning and analysis (FP&A), financial reporting and internal controls. Direct the annual budgeting process and multi-year financial forecasting and planning, in partnership with the CEO and senior leadership. Provide financial analysis and insight to guide strategic, operational and investment decisions, and monitor organizational performance against budget. Oversee the annual audit, cash management and financial compliance.
